references.text: Also describes the burnt offering as a 'fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה)
Same wording about a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord regarding the burnt offering of birds
Aaron's sons shall burn the offering on the altar as a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord
Describes the wood on the altar and the fire that must be kept burning for the offerings
The burnt offering is described as a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the Lord
Refers to the fire on the altar and the pleasing aroma to the Lord
Fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord regarding the daily burnt offering
Paul uses the image of Christ's sacrifice as a pleasing aroma to God (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας), alluding to Old Testament sacrificial language
Describes the common liturgical action where priests place the offering on top of the wood on the altar, illustrating the standardization of the sacrificial procedure.
